By @thm-dist-mle,
an approximate 95% [confidence interval](inference.qmd#def-confidence-interval)
for the $k$th parameter $\theta_k$ is

$$
\hth_k \pm z_{0.975} \times \HSE{\hth_k}
$$

where $\hth_k$ is the $k$th entry of $\hthml$
and $z_{\beta}$ is the $\beta$ quantile of the standard Gaussian distribution
($z_{0.975} \approx 1.96$).
This interval is called a **Wald** confidence interval.
